_meta.source: gszep, "Six safety conditions for upcoming laws" (2026)
_meta.scoring: Team heuristic, not from the source. Each condition is backed by one or more levers. A 'host' lever means the law binds whatever is hosted on the bloc's territory: its strength is the bloc's combined share of that stage. A 'chokepoint' lever means the bloc can attach the condition to exports of an input the world needs: its strength is the bloc's share of the strongest such stage. A condition's score is the strongest of its levers.
_meta.limits: Market share is not leverage by itself: a share only bites if the bloc acts together, the input is hard to replace, and the bloc will accept the cost of using it. The thresholds are a judgement call, shown so readers can disagree.

conditions.name: Testing before release
conditions.text: Evaluators from a recognised AI safety institute in any participating country may test a model trained or hosted there before release.

levers.why: Models trained or served on the bloc's territory fall under its law.
Chip inputs can be licensed on condition that buyers accept testing.

conditions.name: Shared serious-incident definition
conditions.text: One definition of a serious incident, with reports going to every participant.

levers.why: Reporting duties bind operators running systems on the bloc's territory.

conditions.name: Protected model weights
conditions.text: Weights trained or stored in the country meet a common security standard.

levers.why: Only weights stored on the bloc's territory are covered.

conditions.name: Continuity for essential users
conditions.text: Government and critical-infrastructure users keep access to locally hosted models in a crisis.

levers.why: Needs local hosting under a contract that survives withdrawal.

conditions.name: Known chip locations
conditions.text: Operators can show where their advanced chips are; export licences for chips and key inputs carry the same condition.

levers.why: Export licences on chips and their inputs can require location reporting.
Chips installed on the bloc's territory can be required to report location.

conditions.name: Local off-switch, with due process
conditions.text: Operators can isolate or stop a workload on a lawful order of the host country, with notice and review.

levers.why: A host can only switch off what runs on its territory.
